title: Kereta Sia Bah
mood: cheeky outrage, all bark and no bite
subject: a cousin who borrowed your Myvi for one day and brought it back a week later from Kudat
caption: Sabahan pop-rock band sound with Sabah Malay slang, radio-friendly. Twin electric guitars, one playing a clean chorus-pedal riff through the verses and both switching to crunchy overdrive in the chorus, a Hammond-style organ pumping chords, an electric bass locked to the kick, and straight-eighth rock drums opening up the hi-hat in the chorus. Live band in a medium room, guitars panned wide, organ in the middle, the lead vocal forward and dry. High-energy male lead in a bright upper register, cheeky and storytelling, with gang-shout answers in the chorus and a big singalong outro. 128 BPM, E major. Cheeky outrage, all bark and no bite. No autotune, no trap 808s, no drum machine, no moody alt-rock fuzz, no ballad slowdown.
lyrics:
[Intro - clean chorus-pedal guitar riff and drum fill]

[Verse 1]
Isnin lepas sepupu sia datang, senyum lebar macam baru dapat gaji
"Pinjam kereta sehari ja, sia pigi Tuaran hantar barang"
Sia kasi kunci, sia kasi minyak penuh
Sekarang sudah Ahad, telefon pun dia inda angkat

[Pre-Chorus]
Tiba-tiba Facebook dia naik gambar
Myvi sia di Hujung Borneo, ada orang berdiri atas bumbung

[Chorus]
Kereta sia bah! (Kereta dia bah!)
Sehari ko cakap, sudah enam hari
Kereta sia bah! (Kereta dia bah!)
Balik nanti ko basuh, ko isi, ko bayar saman

[Verse 2]
Isnin pagi kereta balik, pasir penuh dalam karpet
Ada sebiji kelapa muda bergolek bawah kerusi belakang
Radio sia tersangkut di stesen yang sia inda kenal
Dia hulur sepuluh ringgit, "Untuk minyak, bah, jangan marah"

[Bridge - guitars drop out, drums and gang vocal only]
Sia mau marah, tapi dia bawa ikan masin Kudat satu plastik
Mak sia sudah senyum - habis, sia kalah lagi

[Chorus]
Kereta sia bah! (Kereta dia bah!)
Sehari ko cakap, jadi tujuh hari
Kereta sia bah! (Kereta dia bah!)
Bulan depan dia pinjam lagi, sia kasi lagi, palui!

[Outro - singalong over open hi-hat]
Kunci sia mana, bah?
Bawah tikar, kunun!
